resolution: Fixed: summary no longer asserts a disclosure duty on optional add-ons (only government taxes require pre-purchase disclosure). Sonnet CONFIRMED.
notes: Audited against data/bill-text/119-HR-1479.txt (Introduced-in-House, IH) — full read, 13,555 chars, no referencedSources. versionChanges reports Introduced->Engrossed unchanged, so IH text governs. ONE material finding: summary asserts optional add-ons 'must be disclosed before the final purchase' — the bill's only pre-final-purchase disclosure duty (2(a)(1)(C)) is scoped strictly to government taxes/fees/assessments; optional products/services carry no disclosure duty (2(a)(2) only permits their display). Secondary minor issues: (1) gaps[1] says the tax disclosure has no specified prominence, but the 2(a)(1) chapeau requires it be done 'clearly, conspicuously, and prominently' (format specifics genuinely unspecified, so half-true); (2) top_lines[1] gives unsourced illustrative examples (parking/breakfast/travel insurance); (3) likelihoodReason carries the usual extrinsic framing (Calendar No. 60, bipartisan/industry-lobbying characterizations) corroborated only by metadata, not bill text. Three minor omissions: 2(a)(3) indemnification carve-out, 2(d)(9) sub-30-day short-term-rental threshold, 2(d)(4) meeting/banquet/catering exclusion. Stage/vote consistent (Passed House; Voice Vote Passed) — no drift. No figure, entity, or direction-inversion errors found in the substantive prose. sourceStart/sourceEnd left null per task instruction; every sourceSpan is a verbatim single-line substring of the source.
